key_insight: The thesis proposes a unified Riemannian deep learning framework that makes neural modules, architectures, and metrics more general, stable, and efficient across non-Euclidean geometries.
clinical_relevance: This work may improve AI models used on biomedical data with manifold structure, such as genomics, imaging, and signals, by enabling more geometry-aware learning.
method: Generalized batch normalization and multinomial logistic regression to Lie groups, gyrogroups, SPD manifolds, and broader Riemannian manifolds.
Built network models for hyperbolic space, Busemann-based learning, and full-rank correlation matrices.
Designed adaptive SPD geometries, including learnable Log-Euclidean and fast Cholesky-based metrics.
evidence_signal: The methods were theoretically analyzed and evaluated in numerical experiments and applications spanning vision, signal processing, graph learning, and genomics.
watch_item: Geometry-aware layers and metrics can be mathematically elegant but may add implementation complexity and require careful numerical validation on each target manifold.
paper_title: Riemannian Deep Learning:Modules, Networks, and Geometries
